title: A Visit to Claas HQ in Harsewinkel
content: # A Visit to Claas HQ in Harsewinkel. ## In November a trip to Harsewinkel, Germany shows the place where Claas was founded and maintains at its worldwide headquarters today. Harsewinkel, Germany is the worldwide hub for the international farm machinery company Claas. Started by August Claas, today the company makes self-propelled combines for corn, soybeans, rice and small grains; self-propelled forage harvesters; haying equipment; and tractors. Claas has invested in new facilities in Omaha, Neb., Russia, and India with the purpose to producing machines where they will be used. The manufacturing facilities there produce self-propelled forage harvesters, Xerion machines, and combines for western Europe as well as threshing modules for other markets. It takes one day’s time to assembly a combine, and the factory produces 18 to 19 combines a day. There is a one assembly line dedicated to Jaguar forage harvesters, and there are 16 machines on the assembly at a time.

content: We had some rain on and off all day. Next we drove to a town about 30 min away called Harsewinkel where there is a HUGE factory that makes farm equipment and columbines. The tour of the facility was long and detailed. Sadly, this is a vacation period for all of the 12,000 workers, so all of the assembly lines were empty of employees at work. This little knotting device was the beginning of all of this:. Founded in 1913 by August Claas, CLAAS is a family business and one of the market and technology leaders in harvesting technology. The beginnings of the company go back to 1887, when Franz Claas founded a company in Clarholz for the production of milk centrifuges. The official foundation of the company took place in 1913, when the son of Franz Claas, August Claas, informed the responsible office in Herzebrock that he was manufacturing straw binders with two locksmiths and one unskilled worker.

title: The world's most modern combine assembly plant pick's up ...
content: # Excellence Harsewinkel: The world’s most modern combine assembly plant pick’s up speed. *CLAAS has invested €44 million in what is currently the world’s most modern combine harvester production at its Harsewinkel site as part of the SynPro 2020 project. With up to 15,000 individual parts, combine harvesters are among the most complex agricultural machines ever built. Redesigned and rebuilt from scratch within the SynPro 2020 project, the TRION and LEXION combine harvester assembly facility at the CLAAS headquarters in Harsewinkel enables precisely that: unparalleled variety, highly flexible production and uncompromising quality – at state-of-the-art workplaces with significant CO2 savings. **More diverse than ever before: Equipped for the future.**Until 2021, combine harvesters were built on two assembly lines in Harsewinkel. Moreover, the launch of the TRION in summer 2021 called for a fresh approach: it meant that a future production facility would have to build more combines per day and cater to an increasingly wide range of models – but with greater use of identical parts.

It begins with a description of the knotter, an important invention by August Claas that helped bind straw into bales. This allowed the company to grow rapidly starting in 1913 when August and his brothers founded Gebrüder Claas. The early years from 1913-1929 saw the company establish itself in Harsewinkel, Germany after initially starting in Clarholz-Heerde.
